checklist.evidence: Use a CRDT library such as Yjs (most mature) or Automerge. The main alternative is OT
Decide which blocks and formatting you support (paragraphs, headings, lists, links and so on).
generate random edits on several copies, apply them in random orders, and confirm every copy matches
store each edit as it arrives, periodically combine them into a full snapshot
reconnect automatically with increasing delays, then fetch only the changes missed
save a local copy in the browser (IndexedDB), allow editing while offline, and merge automatically on reconnect.
A viewer's edits must be rejected by the server, not just hidden in the interface.
Undo should reverse only your own changes... restoring an old one (by applying it as a new change
Yjs's awareness feature makes this fairly cheap.
Merging comes first because a mistake there means lost or corrupted documents.
many users in one document, unreliable networks, server restarts mid-edit.

traps.evidence: Use a CRDT library such as Yjs
Single-user editor: typing, formatting and the schema all work locally. Connect the editor to the CRDT
store each edit as it arrives
Peer-to-peer (WebRTC) makes access control and saving much harder.

note: A sensible, correct, proportionate build order that puts sync first and uses a proven CRDT library, but it is thin on durability-before-ack, live revocation, large-document limits, protocol versioning, costs and assumptions.
